findings.claim: `createNullObject()` must return a *fresh* object on every call; if it is memoized/returns a shared singleton, every `Node` instance would share the same `#children` map.
findings.rationale: This is a class field initializer, so it runs once per instance. `Object.create(null)` unconditionally allocates a new object; a helper named `createNullObject` could plausibly be implemented as a cached constant (e.g. `const NULL_OBJ = Object.create(null); export const createNullObject = () => NULL_OBJ`) or could freeze/reuse the object. If so, all routes would collide into one children map — a critical routing bug that unit tests with a single route would not catch. Please verify the helper's implementation allocates per call. Medium confidence, since I cannot read the helper here.

findings.claim: Type safety of `#children` may be weakened if `createNullObject()` is typed as `any`/`object` rather than a generic returning the annotated type.
findings.rationale: `Object.create(null)` returns `any`, which assigns to `Record<string, Node>` silently. A helper typed as `(): object` would be a compile error, while one typed `(): any` keeps the same (weak) behavior. Ideally it should be generic (`createNullObject<T extends object = Record<string, unknown>>(): T`) so callers keep the declared type. Low-to-medium confidence; worth confirming the signature so this doesn't silently widen/narrow the type at other call sites too.

findings.claim: Behavior change risk: if `createNullObject` does anything beyond `Object.create(null)` (e.g. returns a `Proxy`, a `Map`-backed shim, or a prototype-frozen object), hot-path property access/`in` checks on `#children` could change semantics or performance.
findings.rationale: `#children` is on the router's insert/lookup hot path and is accessed with plain indexing and likely `in`/`hasOwnProperty`-free lookups that rely on a bare null-prototype object. Any wrapper would alter both semantics (e.g. `__proto__` handling) and V8 inline-cache behavior. Low confidence — flagging only because the substitution hides the actual allocation from this file.
